passage:
A child asked a smart speaker for help with homework. The speaker gave a quick answer, but the child copied it without understanding.
His father asked him to explain the answer. He could not.
They used the speaker again, this time asking for examples and simpler explanations. Then the child solved a similar problem by himself.
The father said the tool was useful only when it helped thinking continue.
A smart speaker can answer quickly, but learning is not the same as receiving sound. Students must turn answers into understanding.
The difference between help and shortcut often depends on what happens after the first answer.
